Here's what's stored locally for October 1–3, 2026. Only step counts are available for those dates.

**Daily steps**

| Date | Fitbit | Google |
|---|---|---|
| Oct 1 | 9,000 | 1,000 |
| Oct 2 | (no record) | 2,000 |
| Oct 3 | (no record) | 3,000 |

**Provider selection and double-counting**

- Fitbit has one day (Oct 1). Google has all three days, so I used Google as the single source for the three-day total. That gives **6,000 steps** across Oct 1–3.
- On Oct 1 the two providers disagree (9,000 vs. 1,000). I didn't add them, because they measure the same steps and adding them would count the same day twice. Taking Fitbit's 9,000 for Oct 1 instead would give 14,000 total. That number is not a sum of both providers.
- Which provider you trust for Oct 1 is your call. The Google value looks low next to Fitbit's, so the two may be measuring differently or one may be incomplete. I can't tell which from the local data alone.

**Limitations**

- Local data contains only daily step totals. There's no sleep, heart rate, exercise, or other category for these dates, so I can't summarize those.
- The records carry a parser tag of "eval-synthetic." That suggests they may be test or synthetic data rather than your real device readings. Please check this before relying on the numbers.
- The Fitbit connection isn't currently set up, and the legacy Fitbit Web API is scheduled to shut off on 2026-10-30. Re-syncing from Fitbit may not work after that date.
